newsitem.title: GERMANY: EMU failure would put it back a generation -Santer.
newsitem.headline: EMU failure would put it back a generation -Santer.

text.p: European Commission President Jacques Santer said in an interview published on Thursday that currency union must go ahead on time according to the Maastricht criteria, and that failure would put the idea back a generation.
"I am decidedly in favour of adherence to the criteria and also for adherence to the schedule as it was set down in the (Maastricht) Treaty," Santer told the German daily Die Welt.
"(Up to 1998) we must have our eyes on only one goal: working on fulfilling the (economic) criteria, so that as many states as possible can take part."
Santer was asked what the consequences would be if the start of the planned EU single currency was postponed from 1999.
"A postponement would have serious consequences, not only economic ones but also political ones," he said.
"You can't just stop the clock for a couple of hours or a month as they do in agricultural policy. It would take a whole generation before the subject was back on the agenda."
